docs.title: DataCatalog
docs.text:
A small, dependency-free data catalog for Go: a model that describes which entities and fields an application stores and how each one is classified, for use by query guards, privacy tooling and documentation generators.

  • Model and validation reference
  • Erasure strategies

The package depends only on the standard library. Adapters for ORMs and query guards live in their own modules.

docs.title: Erasure Strategies
docs.text:
The erasure of a field says what privacy tooling does with its value when the data subject is erased.

Strategy Effect clear Set the value to its zero value or NULL. tombstone Replace the value with a fixed marker, keeping the row shape. hash Replace the value with a one-way hash, e.g. to keep uniqueness. delete_row Remove the whole row. shred Destroy the key that protects the value (crypto-shredding). retain Keep the value. A retain_reason is required.

The catalog records the strategy; it does not execute it. Executing erasure is the job of privacy tooling built on the catalog.

Entity-level flags interact with erasure: a hold_applicable entity may need erasure suspended while a hold is in force, and a versioned entity keeps history rows that must be treated with the same strategy as current rows.

docs.title: Entity
docs.text: Field Meaning name Entity name, unique in the catalog. owner Team or component responsible for the entity. description Free text. subject_key Name of the field that identifies the data subject. privacy_scope The entity is subject to access and erasure requests. hold_applicable Legal holds can apply to its rows. Entity-level. versioned The entity keeps row history. Entity-level. retention Free-text retention note. fields The entity's fields, in declaration order.

docs.title: Field
docs.text: Field Meaning name Field name, unique in the entity. description Free text. type Optional coarse type: string, number, bool, time, json, bytes. visibility Required: public or internal. There is no default. pii Personal data about the data subject. secret Credential or key material. Implies internal. erasure Strategy applied on erasure; see Erasure strategies. retain_reason Required when erasure is retain. export Included in data-subject access exports.

docs.title: Audiences
docs.text:
Audience Sees application Public, non-secret fields. internal Every field.

Field.AllowedInQuery(allowPII) is stricter and meant for query guards: internal and secret fields are always blocked, PII fields only when allowPII is true. Catalog.AllowedInQuery(entity, field, allowPII) additionally denies unknown entities and fields.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Catalog.Validate() returns a *ValidationError holding every Problem (entity, field, Rule, message), or nil. Use errors.As to inspect it.

Rule Triggered when name_required Catalog, entity or field name is empty. name_unique Two entities share a name, or two fields of one entity do. visibility_required Visibility is unset or not public/internal. type_invalid A set type is not a known type. erasure_invalid A set erasure is not a known strategy. secret_internal A secret field is not internal. subject_key_required A privacy-scope entity has PII fields but no subject_key. subject_key_unknown subject_key does not name a field of the entity. pii_erasure_required A PII field in a privacy-scope entity has no erasure. retain_reason_required erasure is retain without a retain_reason.

docs.title: File format
docs.text: JSON only. Decoding rejects unknown properties, so a misspelled classification is an error rather than a silent default. Output is stable: entities are sorted by name; fields keep declaration order. The schema is at schema/datacatalog.schema.json.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text: • A dependency-free Go model for describing which entities and fields an application stores and how each is classified, with validation and a query-guard predicate

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Catalog, entity and field model: visibility (public or internal), independent pii and secret tags, erasure strategy, export flag, subject key, privacy scope, hold applicability, versioning and retention note (cacd103)
  • Validate reports every problem at once, with rule identifiers: explicit visibility, secret implies internal, subject key required and known, erasure required for personal data in privacy scope, retain reason required, unique names (41993e1)
  • Audience filtering (VisibleTo, VisibleFields) and default-deny query predicates (AllowedInQuery) that always block internal and secret fields and block personal data unless allowed (48c2845)
  • JSON load and save with stable ordering, Merge that reports conflicting entity definitions, and a Markdown renderer for documentation (7e9e63d)
  • JSON Schema generated from the Go types and embedded, with a test that fails when the committed schema drifts (2aa1cb3)
  • Guides: model and validation reference, and erasure strategies (4865e98)

docs.title: Release Notes v0.1.0
docs.text: Release Date: October 10, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The first release of DataCatalog, a dependency-free Go model for describing which entities and fields an application stores and how each one is classified. It is meant to be consumed by query guards, privacy tooling and documentation generators, so that one definition answers "what data do we hold, who may see it, and what rules apply to it".

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Fields have an explicit visibility (public or internal) and two independent tags, pii and secret, so a display name, a logged IP address and a password hash are each described accurately.
  • secret implies internal, and visibility is never defaulted: an unclassified field is an error, not a public one.
  • Validation reports every problem at once, with a rule identifier for each.
  • Query guards can ask one question, AllowedInQuery, which is default-deny and always blocks internal and secret fields.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go get github.com/grokify/datacatalog@v0.1.0

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
• Catalog, Entity and Field.
  • Entity-level attributes: owner, subject key, privacy scope, hold applicability, versioning and a retention note.
  • Field-level attributes: type, visibility, pii, secret, erasure strategy (clear, tombstone, hash, delete_row, shred, retain), retain reason and export flag.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Validate on a catalog or an entity returns every problem.
  • Rules: names required and unique, visibility required, secret implies internal, subject key required and known, erasure strategy required for personal data in privacy scope, retain reason required.

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
• VisibleTo and VisibleFields for audiences.
  • AllowedInQuery(allowPII) for query guards.

docs.title: Interchange
docs.text:
• JSON load and save with stable ordering.
  • Merge, which errors on conflicting definitions of one entity.
  • RenderMarkdown for documentation tables.
  • An embedded JSON Schema generated from the Go types.
